question: Can a class-balanced LightGBM with one-hot window features beat a standard random forest on a public residue-window sequence classification task that stands in for linear B-cell epitope prediction?
method: Single stratified 75/25 split (seed 42). Baseline: 300-tree random forest on one-hot window features. Improved: class-balanced LightGBM with 3-fold CV grid over learning rate and leaves, plus isotonic calibration on an inner split. Test set used once; seeds 42-44.

dataset.name: UCI Molecular Biology Splice-junction Gene Sequences (stand-in, not epitope data)

baseline: Standard random forest (300 trees) on one-hot encoded window positions, raw class probabilities.
improved: Class-balanced LightGBM on the same one-hot features, small CV grid over learning rate and num_leaves, isotonic calibration fitted on a 20% inner split of the training data.
notes: Stand-in task: DNA splice-junction windows, not linear B-cell epitopes; results say nothing about epitope prediction. Single split, so variance across splits is not measured. The improved model's final fit uses 80% of training rows (the rest calibrates isotonic). The baseline uses all training rows. Seeds vary model randomness only.
